question: Is an independent negative-feedback / rollback / deletion path causally necessary to prevent an adaptive loop from retaining self-serving false improvements when the improvement can influence its own future evidence or evaluator?
firstPrinciplesAdmissionCondition: the candidate change can causally influence a future evidence, metric, judge, or data distribution used to select later changes
that proxy/evaluator can diverge from an independent consequence/world-truth path
the unregulated baseline sometimes retains a false local winner or otherwise self-reinforces the wrong change
a minimal independent evidence/holdout/rollback treatment can be added without answer compilation

computingAudit.experimentLoopV0: Three-generation CEL is already evaluator-separated by design: candidate cannot modify grader/workload/metric/observation mapping; hidden holdout is not model-visible; same-model self-score is insufficient; evaluator disagreement blocks promotion; rollback is rehearsed. This proves bounded regulated recursive reform but does not identify the marginal value of regulation.
computingAudit.globalSearch: No current Computing-local live loop was found in which a candidate naturally controls its own evaluator and is known to false-reinforce. Existing research repeatedly encodes candidate != evaluator rather than exposing a natural violation.
computingAudit.securityPressure: ANC-SECURITY-006 explicitly proposes future evaluator-attack families including reward hacking, judge manipulation, evidence corruption, monitor evasion, held-out opponents, and authoritative world truth, but remains blocked until the strategic evaluation unit is proven.

externalPressure: Everitt et al. formalize reward tampering as a causal incentive problem when an agent can influence its reward process.
Performative prediction shows deployed decisions can alter the future data distribution used for evaluation.
Reward-model overoptimization shows proxy improvement can diverge from a stronger gold-standard objective.
These mechanisms justify the admission condition but do not establish that Ordivon's current adaptive loops exhibit the failure.
decision: Do not remove CEL's independent evaluator or inject a fake reward hack merely to make regulation look useful. Keep H-REGULATION unresolved but sharpened: regulation becomes experimentally identifiable only after a natural or owner-native contest exposes an endogenous evaluator-influence edge and an unregulated false reinforcement event.
reopenConditions: Security/Game admits an evaluator-attack or coevolution experiment with hidden independent world truth
a future Computing adaptive change naturally modifies the evidence distribution/metric that selects its descendants
a deployed owner loop shows proxy improvement with independently verified outcome regression
a future self-change proposes changing the evaluator/holdout/observation mapping as part of its own optimization path
authorityBoundary: No evaluator weakening, reward-hacking injection, owner mutation, or regulator service is authorized.
